text.p: Time Warner Inc's Time magazine said on Wednesday it is suing Ohio-based online provider CompuServe for at least $3.5 million, for seeking to eliminate Time from its online service and allegedly refusing to make payments due to the magazine.
Time said the suit seeks not less than $3.5 million for CompuServe's repudiation of the two-year contract with Time and asks the court to require CompuServe to continue to provide service.
CompuServe has not yet seen the suit, spokeswoman Gail Whitcomb said.
"As soon as we've seen the suit we will commment," she said.
Time said the suit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio.

Time, which joined CompuServe in March 1996, said it anchors the service's news center and provides both current and archived editorial content from the magazine, as well as a round-the-clock daily news service.

Time, which was previously carried on America Online, said it moved to CompuServe following aggressive efforts by the company that promised Time long-term opportunities and the potential to expand the TIME brand.
Time charged that in January, CompuServe sent Time a notice attempting to renege on its agreement, citing its financial objectives for the coming fiscal year.
Time said it filed its lawsuit following unsuccessful negotiations with CompuServe.
